title: Adaptive Sync-Slab Scheduler for token-wave interleaving and NCCL overlap
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Multi-GPU prefill + decode paths see variable latency due to unsynchronized stage handoffs and suboptimal kernel selection decisions. This manifests as tail latency spikes when NCCL collectives overlap poorly with stage-local compute, and degraded throughput for medium-length sequences (512-2048).

Goal: Implement an adaptive scheduling layer (Sync-Slab Scheduler) that aligns token-wave boundaries across tensor/pipeline stages to increase NCCL overlap during prefill and steady-state decode while providing kernel-selection hints to local runtimes to favor latency-friendly kernels when overlap budgets are tight. The feature should: 1) reduce 95/99th latency for prefills by 15-30% on heterogeneous mGPU clusters, 2) avoid regressions for short sequences, and 3) integrate with existing routing/fallback policies in runtime-1.22.
approach:
High-level: introduce a lightweight coordinator that tracks stage readiness windows (slabs) and assigns token-wave start offsets so adjacent stages interleave compute and comm deterministically. The scheduler emits two artifacts per request: (a) a slab-offset token metadata used by the prefill conductor, and (b) kernel-hint tags (latency-priority | throughput-priority | balanced) that guide local kernel-selection heuristics.

Implementation phases:
- Phase 1: Simulation + heuristics (this ticket) — build a simulator that ingests device bandwidth/latency profiles and synthetic token arrival distributions to validate slab-sizing heuristics.
- Phase 2: Runtime prototype — implement a coordinator service + per-worker slab agent that negotiates offsets over the existing rendezvous channel; add a kernel-hint API surface to the runtime.
- Phase 3: Canary + rollouts — run canaries on dedicated pools with mixed A100/V100 and heterogeneous NVLink topologies; collect latency token traces and NCCL timeline overlays.

Key algorithms: adaptive slab sizing (percentile-based), offset negotiation with bounded staleness, kernel hint resolution using a cost model that weights per-kernel latency, FLOP efficiency, and cache pressure.
tradeoffs:
- Deterministic interleaving increases scheduler complexity and requires extra metadata on requests (slab offset). We trade a small extra per-request metadata field for better overlap and lower tail latency.
- Kernel hinting can bias against highest-throughput kernels in favor of latency-stable kernels; risk of lowered aggregate throughput in high-batch workloads. We'll gate hinting behind a per-route policy.
- Coordinator adds a control-plane dependency; to mitigate, the per-worker slab agent can fallback to local default behavior on coordinator failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- Sync-Slab simulator validated against synthetic traces; documented slab-sizing heuristics (confluence doc).
- Runtime prototype merges: coordinator + slab-agent + kernel-hint resolver.
- Canary results: 95th latency reduction >= 15% and 99th >= 10% vs baseline for sequences 512-2048 on test cluster; no more than 5% throughput regression for batch-heavy workloads.
- Automated tests for slab negotiation correctness and kernel-hint resolution.
- Observability: per-request slab offset recorded in tracing and per-route dashboard updated.
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with infra and runtime owners. Agreed simulator input format and metrics (P50/P95/P99, NCCL overlap ratio, per-stage idle time).
2026-03-04: Simulator prototype completed. Early runs show potential 22% P95 improvement on homogeneous NVLink topo with slab size tuned to 32 tokens. Attached charts in Confluence.

2026-03-06: Design review with PM + SRE. Decided to implement kernel-hint as soft hints (non-blocking) and expose per-route opt-in flag for now. Added requirement: coordinator must be able to operate with best-effort staleness <= 100ms.

2026-03-09: Runtime prototype PR opened for slab-agent and kernel-hint schema. Initial unit tests passing. Performance harness scheduled for 2026-03-12. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
notes: Next steps: run the performance harness across heterogeneous testbeds (mixed GPU types and cross-rack IB), amplify dataset with realistic prefix distributions from production traces (anonymized). If canary metrics meet targets, schedule integration with rollout policies and add a 'latency-first' knob in Console. Investigate combining slab scheduling with prefix-KV caching heuristics (possible follow-up: ENG-941015).
